title: Building lines with long notes, many findings, or a deleted work order
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', on the build under test; ShopCoach is enabled and the shop has at least one labor type.
  2. Two completed inspections to build from: one with a very long technician note, one with about thirty Monitor or Not OK findings (seed via a template with ~30 checkbox fields all marked Not OK).
  3. A second browser (or private window) signed in as another user who can close, delete or reopen the work order or the inspection.
custom_steps:
1. Build from the long-note inspection and check the drafted line reflects the whole note (nothing cut off).
2. Build from the thirty-finding inspection and check there is no cap and no extra confirmation, and that every finding is drafted (a set too large to draft at once is split across runs, not dropped).
3. Start a build choosing 'add to the open work order', then in the second browser close or delete that work order before you confirm; check the result matches the expected result below.
4. Repeat, using the second browser to reopen the inspection, and to delete the built lines versus delete the work order; check each result against the expected result below.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A very long note is given to ShopCoach whole, rather than truncated before it is read.
  • An inspection with thirty flagged findings builds without a cap or extra confirmation; a run too large to draft at once is split rather than the surplus dropped.
  • If the chosen open work order was closed by someone else in the meantime, the system tells the user and creates nothing.
  • If the run-on work order is deleted before the user confirms, the build fails without creating a partial result.
  • If two users draft from the same inspection at once, the drafting itself duplicates nothing; duplication happens only if both press Add Lines, which is accepted and recoverable.
  • If the inspection is reopened by someone else while a draft is on screen, the draft stays usable and any lines already added are kept.
  • If the lines were built onto a new work order and that work order is later deleted, the inspection counts as needing a work order again, while the inspection itself is unaffected.
  • Reversing an invoice does not change the inspection's state, because the work order and its lines still exist.
  • If the lines built from an inspection are deleted while the work order remains, the inspection stays actioned and does not return to needing a work order.
  • If the run-on work order is deleted, the inspection survives it and stays listed on the asset with a dash in its work order column; any lines added to that work order are gone with it and the inspection counts as needing a work order again.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9100 (S2 — Turn findings into work order lines); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S2; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-E2: “If a note is very long, it is given to ShopCoach whole rather than truncated before it is read”
  • S2-E3: “An inspection with thirty flagged findings is built without a cap and without an extra confirmation. If the assistant cannot draft that many in one run, the run is split rather than the surplus findings being dropped (S15-R14)”
  • S2-E4: “If the user chose to add lines to the open work order and it was closed by someone else in the meantime, the system tells the user and creates nothing”
  • S2-E5: “If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted before the user confirms, the build fails without creating a partial result”
  • S2-E6: “If two users draft from the same inspection at once, nothing is duplicated by the drafting itself, because a draft is not a work order line. Duplication happens only if both press Add Lines, which is accepted and recoverable”
  • S2-E7: “If the inspection is reopened by someone else while a draft is on screen, the draft stays usable and any lines already added are kept”
  • S2-E9: “If the lines were built onto a new work order and that work order is later deleted, the inspection counts as needing a work order again. The inspection itself is unaffected, because it belongs to the work order it was run on”
  • S2-E10: “Reversing an invoice does not change the inspection's state, because the work order and its lines still exist”
  • S2-E11: “If the lines built from an inspection are deleted while the work order remains, the inspection stays actioned and does not return to needing a work order. Deleting a work order is usually a correction; deleting a line is somebody who read the proposed work and decided against it, and re-raising the flag would ask them to do it again”
  • S2-E12: “If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted, the inspection survives it (S5-R21) and stays listed on the asset with a dash in its work order column. Where the lines had been added to that same work order they are gone with it, and the inspection counts as needing a work order again”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.
